name: Titanic Passenger Survival
tagline: Predict passenger survival on the RMS Titanic from demographic and ticket records.
description:
Historical passenger manifest records from the April 1912 sinking of the RMS Titanic, curated from Encyclopedia Titanica sources by Thomas Cason and Frank E. Harrell Jr. and packaged in the canonical 891-passenger training subset popularized by Kaggle and seaborn.

Widely used as an introductory binary classification benchmark, Titanic combines mixed numeric, boolean, and categorical features, explicit missing values across age (177), cabin deck (688), and embarkation port (2), derived duplicate columns that teach target leakage hygiene ('alive', 'class'), and stark demographic survival disparities shaped by 'women and children first' evacuation norms and third-class structural barriers.

targetCandidates.description: Predict whether the passenger survived the sinking (1 = Survived, 0 = Did not survive).
Predict passenger ticket class (1st, 2nd, or 3rd) from fare, family size, and demographics.

columns.name: survived
columns.description: Survival outcome of the passenger in the 1912 sinking.

columns.name: pclass
columns.description: Proxy for socioeconomic status and shipboard deck location based on ticket tier.

columns.name: sex
columns.description: Recorded biological sex of the passenger.

columns.name: age
columns.description: Passenger age in years (fractional if infant under 1 year; missing for 177 passengers).

columns.name: sibsp
columns.description: Number of siblings or spouses traveling aboard the Titanic with the passenger.

columns.name: parch
columns.description: Number of parents or children traveling aboard the Titanic with the passenger.

columns.name: fare
columns.description: Ticket fare paid in 1912 British pounds sterling (often shared across multi-person group tickets; 0.0 indicates complimentary or employee passage).

columns.name: embarked
columns.description: Port where the passenger boarded the RMS Titanic.

columns.name: class
columns.description: Text duplicate of the integer-coded 'pclass' column added in seaborn's export.
columns.exclusionReason: Exact string duplicate of 'pclass' (unchecked by default and auto-disabled when predicting 'pclass').

columns.name: who
columns.exclusionReason: Derived composite of 'sex' and 'age' (optional engineered feature unchecked by default to avoid redundancy).

columns.name: adult_male
columns.description: Boolean indicator equal to True when passenger is male and age >= 16 (or age unknown).
columns.exclusionReason: Derived indicator from 'sex' and 'age' unchecked by default to keep primary features unconfounded.

columns.name: deck
columns.description: Ship deck letter (A through G) extracted from cabin number; missing for 688 of 891 passengers.
columns.exclusionReason: Missing in 77.2% of records (primarily 3rd-class passengers without recorded cabin numbers).

columns.name: embark_town
columns.description: Full town name duplicate of the single-letter 'embarked' port column.
columns.exclusionReason: Exact string duplicate of the 'embarked' column.

columns.name: alive
columns.description: Text duplicate ('yes'/'no') of the binary 'survived' target column.
columns.exclusionReason: Exact string duplicate of the 'survived' target column.

columns.name: alone
columns.description: Derived boolean indicator equal to True when both 'sibsp' and 'parch' equal 0.
columns.exclusionReason: Derived indicator from 'sibsp' and 'parch' unchecked by default to avoid feature redundancy.

warnings: Historical rescue protocols ('women and children first') and shipboard class segregation produce extreme survival disparities (74.2% female vs. 18.9% male; 63.0% 1st class vs. 24.2% 3rd class), illustrating how social norms and structural privilege become encoded in historical data.
Missingness in 'deck' (77.2%) and 'age' (19.9%) is not missing completely at random (MCAR): 3rd-class passengers were disproportionately less likely to have recorded cabin numbers or ages.
